output.title: Check data residency before you automate
output.body:
Before you automate a workflow, make data residency the first control, not a footnote. Residency just means where the data is allowed to live and move: on your own systems, in a specific country, or inside a vendor service. For an owner-operator, the useful question is not “can AI do this?” but “which parts of this workflow are allowed to leave my environment at all?”

Take one recurring process you already handle by hand, such as customer-data entry, invoice processing, or lead follow-up. Treat it as an example, not a promise. List the fields you would not want to hand to a third party: payment details, personal data, internal pricing, or anything a supplier agreement keeps in place. Then read the tool’s service terms and data-handling docs. The owner decides any legal or contractual requirement; you are just checking the boundary before you pilot.

That is the threshold: what can move, and what must stay put. If most of the workflow can move and the tool’s terms fit, a pilot may make sense. If the data must stay local, you are looking at a self-hosted or tightly integrated approach. Less glamorous than a demo video, but more useful on Monday.
